answer:
In causal attention, a token's hidden state and later-layer KV representations depend on preceding context. Changing an early system-prompt token therefore makes the suffix's cached states inconsistent, even if all later user-visible tokens are textually unchanged. Hash-chained prefix caches naturally reject the changed block and its descendants. [1](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/prefix_caching/) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762)

The unchanged prefix before the edit can remain reusable at the cache's block granularity; it is not necessarily the entire cache that becomes invalid. If the edit occurs near the start, almost every later block is affected, which explains the large recomputation in multi-turn workflows. Append new information when semantically appropriate and version stable prompts deliberately. Never reuse stale KV values solely because the conversation's final text looks similar or because the edit seems minor to a human.
